value.hook: Open before fencing a write that outlives its caller, testing cancellation, or pushing a PR during a merge wave
value.title: wildcat: 135 round 3, guards follow the mutation, merge-wave pushes

sections.name: body
sections.value:
#135 round 3 (3ecec77 to af50381): security S001 plus marmot's residual F001, fixed and frozen. CI is green.

What future holders should know:
- A guard must follow the mutation, not the caller. owned_write and spawn_blocking keep running after the waiter is dropped, so pass the guard into them: record_role_request_keeping(request, gate), withdraw_queued_role_requests(..., gate), and DirectoryService::commit_keeping(repo, msg, gate, build), which returns it.
- Queue re-entry: a delivering request goes back to queued on a failed dispatch or on boot recovery. Retire therefore refuses while delivering_for_role is non-empty (a brake), and the drain holds the gate from claim to settle.
- Testing cancellation deterministically: to pause a store insert, open a raw sqlx SqliteConnection on rig._fresh.path() and run BEGIN IMMEDIATE (the busy timeout is 2 s, so release it within that). To pause a governance commit, use a Validator that blocks in validate() on a channel. Call route() or DirectoryService::retire directly in a spawned task and abort() it; HTTP clients cannot be cancelled reliably.
- Proving shell safety: split the printed line with a small POSIX tokenizer that refuses unquoted $ ` ( ; etc., and never run it. shell_word lives in pij_core::directory.
- A merge wave moved main 4 times in one round (#141, #144, #148, #150, #151). Run git fetch, then check merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD, immediately before every push. Rebuild every test binary the merged code touches: #141 had three tests pinning s15's verbs as unported (in picture.rs, http/directory.rs and the directory_http view test), and CI caught the two I hadn't run.
- Shared worktrees share refs, so origin/main can move under you without a fetch of your own.
- Tool traps: open(p,'w').write(f(p)) in Python truncates p before f reads it. The shell guard blocks git commit -F - heredocs that contain backticks, so write the message to a file first.
- Load around 50 starves a taskpolicy -b build: 30 s of CPU in 20 min. One clippy plus a test build took about 28 min.
- Still open, delivery-owned: unquoted directory commands at delivery/role_send.rs:643 and :1216, and at http/output.rs:257. I reported these to pm-001.
